🔥 claude-motion | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To enable AI coding agents to autonomously generate high-quality motion graphics and video content from simulations or design specifications.
✨ Key Features: • Motion design rules and presets for agents • Self-review loop for frame analysis and correction • Integrated sound engine for audio generation (typing, clicks, whooshes, etc.)
📖 Summary: Claude-motion is a JavaScript toolkit that empowers coding agents to create sophisticated motion graphics and web-based simulations. It provides agents with 'taste' by teaching them motion design principles, enabling self-review of frames, and integrating a sound engine for audio generation. The toolkit also facilitates the conversion of web simulations into high-frame-rate videos.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 stargazer | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Creating shareable social media assets (cards and videos) to celebrate GitHub project milestones like reaching star count goals.
✨ Key Features: • Generate cinematic 1600x900 social cards • Create 60fps MP4 loops • In-browser video export via WebCodecs • 100% client-side and private processing • Live real-time previews
📖 Summary: Stargazer is a browser-based tool that transforms GitHub stargazers and contributors into visually appealing social media cards and animated MP4 loops. It focuses on client-side processing for privacy and real-time previews, allowing users to celebrate project milestones with custom designs.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 Animator | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Creating explainer videos automatically from text prompts for educational or informational content.
✨ Key Features: • Generates narrated whiteboard explainer videos from text prompts • AI-powered scriptwriting, scene drawing, and narration • Synchronizes animation with spoken narration • Supports custom images and audio for video creation • No GPU required, runs locally on CPU
📖 Summary: Animator is a Python tool that automatically generates narrated, hand-drawn whiteboard explainer videos from a simple text prompt. It leverages AI to write scripts, draw scenes, record narration, and animate elements in sync with the spoken words.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 shellfirm | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: Preventing dangerous or unintended shell command execution by humans and AI agents.
✨ Key Features: • 100+ patterns across 9 ecosystems • Support for 8 shells (Zsh, Bash, Fish, etc.) • Context-aware escalation (SSH, root, production environments) • Safe alternative command suggestions • Configurable severity levels
📖 Summary: Shellfirm acts as a safety net for terminal commands, protecting against accidental or malicious execution by both humans and AI agents. It intercepts commands, analyzes their potential risk, and can present challenges or suggest safer alternatives before execution.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 ggwave | C++
🎯 Primary Use Case: Enabling data communication between devices using audible or ultrasonic sound waves, particularly useful for air-gapped systems or simple device pairing.
✨ Key Features: • Tiny data-over-sound library • FSK-based transmission protocol • Error correction codes (ECC) for robustness • Supports RAW waveform generation and analysis • Works with any audio backend via callbacks
📖 Summary: ggwave is a tiny C++ library that enables data transmission through sound waves, including ultrasound. It uses a simple FSK modulation and error correction codes to ensure robust communication between air-gapped devices, supporting various platforms like Arduino and Python.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
